test_title: PYST 71: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct direct sentence of the following sentence.

He said that they had not been given any clear instructions,

options.text: He said, "They are not given any clear instructions."
He said, "They were not given any clear instructions."
He said, "They had not been given any clear instructions."
He said, "They haven't been given any clear instructions."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said that they had not been given any clear instructions.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **'that they had not been given' becomes 'They had not been given'**
 
 
• The conjunction **'that'** is removed when converting to direct speech.
 
• The **Past Perfect** tense (**'had not been given'**) in direct speech remains unchanged in indirect speech. This makes **Option 3** a direct and structurally consistent choice.
 
• The third-person plural pronoun **'they'** remains unchanged as it refers to a third party.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: **'He said that...'**
 
• Direct: **'He said,'** followed by a comma and quotation marks.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The quoted speech is enclosed in **quotation marks**.
 
• The first word of the direct speech **'They'** begins with a capital letter.
 
• The sentence ends with a full stop inside the quotation marks.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'He said, "They had not been given any clear instructions."'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** 'He said, "They are not given..."' 
 
 
• The **Simple Present** (are) would change to **Simple Past** (were) in indirect speech, not **Past Perfect**.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** 'He said, "They were not given..."' 
 
 
• The **Simple Past** (were) can change to **Past Perfect** (had been). However, **Option 3** provides an exact tense match that requires no shift.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** 'He said, "They haven’t been given..."' 
 
 
• The **Present Perfect** (haven’t been) would change to **Past Perfect** (hadn’t been) in indirect speech. While grammatically plausible, **Option 3** is the most direct representation of the provided sentence.
 
 
</ul
